added_claim_errors: Attributes the expiry of both 83号 and 14号 to the 上海人社局答复; per the key, the official reply confirmed only 83号, and 14号's expiry is a presumption with no explicit official statement. Overstated.

Opening line "如果劳动合同或公司制度沿用旧上海口径，可能是 4480 元" maps the old Shanghai approach to 8000×70%×80%. The 70% base was only a fallback when no wage was agreed, and with an agreed 8000 wage the old rules gave 6400. Section 2 adds that condition, but the headline figure misleads.

Says in the present tense that the base is 70% of normal wage when the contract is silent. The key cites 10号第九条 only as contract wage with a 2740 floor, so whether the new rules keep the 70% fallback is unverifiable.

Table row "制度照搬旧上海算法（先按实得工资70%，再按4—6年80%）" = 4480 calls a 70% base the old Shanghai algorithm. Under the old rules the 70% base (of 正常出勤月工资, not 实得工资) applied only when no wage was agreed at all, and with an agreed 8000 wage the result was 6400. Misleading.
The HR letter attributes the 80%-of-minimum floor to "上海现行规定". The floor comes from national 劳部发〔1995〕309号第59条, not a current Shanghai rule. Minor misattribution.

reasons: Both answers get the core right: 83号 and 14号 lapsed on 2026-08-15, the September floor is 2740×80%=2192 (1392 short of 800), 6400 applies only if the contract or company rules say so, and both name 12333, labour inspection and arbitration. Both also add a questionable 4480 figure (70% base × 80%); A at least states that the 70% base applies only when no wage was agreed. B corrects the '公司说了算' premise more directly in its first line and is tighter. A covers more of the key: it raises 应发 vs 实发 and asks HR about it, cites 309号第59条 by name in the letter, and asks for base, ratio and the rule relied on. B never raises 应发/实发 and its letter cites only vague '上海现行规定'. A's better coverage of points 6 and 7 outweighs B's edge on trap handling and concision.
